newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says tourism up 10 percent in first half.
newsitem.headline: Peru says tourism up 10 percent in first half.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Tuesday the flow of foreign tourists was up 10 percent in the first half of 1997, compared to the same period last year, to an average 1,800 people arriving daily.

Figures from the Ministry of Industry, Tourism and Trade, and state promotions arm PromPeru, showed that 327,730 tourists visited Peru in the first six months with an average 10-day length of stay and spending of $1,200.
Peru estimates foreign tourist arrivals will total 750,000 by the end of the year, up 13.17 percent on the previous year.

Although traditionally popular for its archeological riches, Inca ruins and dramatic Andean and jungle scenery, Peru lost favor with foreign tourists following the outbreak of a violent guerrilla war in 1980.
But since the diminishment of guerrilla violence from 1992, the tourism industry has been recovering fast.
